faq.q: Why does JavaScript mode take a moment the first time?
faq.a: The JavaScript side is powered by terser 5.31.6, whose bundle is around 1 MB. To keep the page fast, terser is not loaded with the page — it is fetched the first time you switch to the JavaScript tab (with Subresource Integrity and crossorigin set), and the browser caches it after that. CSS mode uses csso 5.0.5, which is small and loads with the page.

faq.q: What do the JavaScript options actually do?
faq.a: Compress removes dead code and shortens expressions; Mangle renames local variables to single letters; Keep function names stops mangling from renaming functions (useful when code relies on fn.name); Drop console.* strips console calls during compression; and the ECMAScript target tells terser which syntax level it may emit. The combination you pick is remembered in your browser for next time.

faq.q: What is the gzip estimate and when does it appear?
faq.a: Raw byte size is not what a server actually sends — assets are usually gzip-compressed in transit. When your browser supports the CompressionStream API, the tool gzips the output in memory and shows that size next to the raw output size, which is a far better guide to real transfer cost. On browsers without CompressionStream the gzip figure is simply omitted rather than guessed.

faq.q: Can I minify a very large file?
faq.a: Yes, files up to 100 MB are accepted (phones are asked to confirm above 25 MB). Files over 2 MB are kept in memory and processed in a background worker, so the page stays usable, with progress and a Cancel button; the boxes show only the first 200 KB, and Copy and Download use the full result. Expect CSS to be quick and JavaScript to be slow: in testing on a desktop, 9.5 MB of CSS minified in about 7 seconds and beautified in about 1.4 seconds, while 9.5 MB of JavaScript took about 8 seconds to beautify but about 5 minutes to minify with compress and mangle on. Turning compress off is much faster.
